problem_text:
A logistics coordinator is tasked with assembling a shipment of specialized components to maximize total utility while adhering to a cargo mass restriction.

The components under consideration are:
* Component A: mass 3 units, utility 59 credits
* Component B: mass 29 units, utility 153 credits
* Component C: mass 49 units, utility 181 credits
* Component D: mass 17 units, utility 237 credits
* Component E: mass 2 units, utility 185 credits
* Component F: mass 47 units, utility 174 credits
* Component G: mass 41 units, utility 134 credits
* Component H: mass 23 units, utility 195 credits
* Component I: mass 23 units, utility 202 credits
* Component J: mass 13 units, utility 18 credits
* Component K: mass 26 units, utility 285 credits
* Component L: mass 20 units, utility 215 credits
* Component M: mass 39 units, utility 21 credits
* Component N: mass 35 units, utility 70 credits
* Component O: mass 21 units, utility 22 credits
* Component P: mass 28 units, utility 83 credits
* Component Q: mass 6 units, utility 74 credits
* Component R: mass 4 units, utility 294 credits
* Component S: mass 19 units, utility 110 credits
* Component T: mass 49 units, utility 195 credits
* Component U: mass 16 units, utility 299 credits
* Component V: mass 6 units, utility 124 credits

Furthermore, due to compatibility protocols, exactly one of Component A and Component B must be included in the final selection.

Should Component C be selected, the effective cargo capacity of the transport vessel is diminished by 10 units.
The vessel's maximum allowable cargo mass is 361 units. The coordinator must determine the optimal set of components to include.
